subject: What does aroma do to my .Last() function?

messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: What does aroma do to my .Last() function?
parts:
I have often run into this problem when I have used aroma previously
in the R environment. If, in my current session, I have not actually
loaded the library, I get the following error when I try to quit:

> q()
Save workspace image? [y/n/c]: n
Error in .Last() : could not find function "finalizeSession"

To exit, I have to run q(runLast=F). This happens both on my windows
machine and on the lbl unix machine that I SSH into.

If the library is loaded in the current session, however, I do not get
this message. This seems to be only for R sessions that I have used
aroma in before (i.e., if I open a fresh R session with no saved
environment information or if I am in a R session where I have never
loaded the aroma package before, this does not seem to happen), but I
think it continues happening everytime I open the session from then
on. I think it may have to do with one of the "R.xxx" utility packages
because I remember getting this message before when I do not think I
had ever loaded aroma, but rather one of these utility functions to
run a function of Ken's last fall. I wound up reinstalling R or
updating or something to get rid of it, but now that I'm using the
aroma package a lot, I'd like to know what this is.

Best,
Elizabeth

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] What does aroma do to my .Last() function?
parts:
Hi.

Maybe it is the NSI ;) Seriously, sorry that you had problems with
this. It is the R.utils package that modifies you .Last() such that
it first calls finalizeSession() and the calls your original .Last(),
which has been renamed to .LastOriginal(). See below for more
details. So, yes, you're right, it is unrelated to aroma.affymetrix.

I'm trying to figure out what is happening because I haven't heard of
this before. One likely scenario could be that you load R.utils, then
store your session (.RData), and then when you start R without loading
R.utils and tries to exit the patched .Last() from the "R.utils"
session is called and you get an error that finalizeSession() cannot
be found. It sounds from you description that this is actually the
case. Note that R.utils do not modify any files or similar, so you
should only see this when you load R.utils.

I will update the "patch" so that 1) it never stops with an error by
using a tryCatch() call, and 2) call R.utils::finalizeSession()
explicitly so that the package does not have to be loaded.

Before that is updated, the quick fix is to do:

.Last <- .LastOriginal

If there is not .LastOriginal, then just do rm(.Last).

Details below.

Sorry about the mess. Thanks for telling me.

Henrik


DETAILS:

The finalizeSession() method defined in R.utils calls "onSessionExit"
hooks (functions). If no hooks are set, nothing extra is done. The
reason for doing all this is to add a general way for packages and
other code to always be called when R exits. I added this in June
2005, and at the same time I asked if there was a similar feature
already in R, but there wasn't, cf.
http://tolstoy.newcastle.edu.au/R/devel/05/06/1206.html. Example of
the modification follows.

% R
> .Last
function() {
if (interactive()) savehistory();
}
> library(R.utils)
Loading required package: R.oo
R.oo v1.2.5 (2006-01-05) successfully loaded. See ?R.oo for help.
R.utils v0.8.3 (2006-11-10) successfully loaded. See ?R.utils for help.
> .Last
function (...)
{
finalizeSession()
if (exists(".LastOriginal", mode = "function"))
.LastOriginal()
}
<environment: 0x02678824>
attr(,"finalizeSession")
[1] TRUE
> .LastOriginal
function() {
if (interactive()) savehistory();
}

STOP. /HB

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: What does aroma do to my .Last() function?
parts:
For the completion of this thread:

I've update R.utils, so that it does not cause the problem in the
first place, and so that it corrects existing problems upon loading.
Thus, if you have a problematic .RData file that loads a faulty
.Last() function, loading R.utils will fix the problem (if the faulty
.Last() was due to R.utils that is).

Until committed to CRAN, the updated R.utils (v 0.8.6) can be installed by:

source("http://www.braju.com/R/hbLite.R")
hbLite("R.utils")

Cheers

Henrik
